name: Seawater fizz bed
subtitle: pulling carbon dioxide out of seawater as bubbles

effects.effect: slightly acidified seawater holds more dissolved carbon dioxide than it should
bubbles start only on rough spots

effect: slightly acidified seawater holds more dissolved carbon dioxide than it should
how: The ocean holds about fifty times more carbon than the air, so taking carbon dioxide out of seawater lets the sea soak up more from the sky. Once seawater is made slightly acidic it is overloaded with dissolved carbon dioxide, but bubbles won't start on their own; running it through a bed of rough glass beads gives the gas millions of starting points, so it fizzes out like opened soda and is collected, with no vacuum pump.
obstacle: Acidifying the seawater and neutralising it again before release takes electricity, and that sets the cost per tonne.
why: Swapping vacuum pumps for free bubble-starting surfaces cuts the energy of ocean carbon capture.
real: Patents describe degassing CO2 from acidified seawater (often with vacuum or membranes) and a lake-degassing patent proposes catalysed nucleation, but no nucleation packed bed for seawater CO2 removal was found.
